\chapter{The model library}\label{doc:model-index}

This is the catalogue of models RAMSES can load. Each family has its own page with
equations, parameters in declaration order, and worked examples. For the record
syntax that references these models, see
\hyperref[ch-sync]{Dynamic Data Records}.

\section{How a Model Name Resolves}\label{model-index:how-a-model-name-resolves}

RAMSES adds the family prefix (\texttt{exc\_}, \texttt{tor\_}, \texttt{inj\_}, \texttt{twop\_}) automatically, so
\texttt{AC1A} and \texttt{exc\_AC1A} are the same model. Names are \textbf{case sensitive}.

A model can be in one of three states, and the tables below say which:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{small}\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3031}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.6969}}
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
State
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Meaning
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Built in} & Handled directly by the family dispatcher, no prefix \\
\textbf{Registered} & Compiled and mapped to a name, callable from a data file \\
\textbf{Not compiled} & Present as source but excluded from the build, so not reachable at all \\
\end{longtable}\end{small}
}

\begin{docsnote}{Every compiled model is reachable}

As of 3.79 every model compiled into the library is mapped to a name and can be
loaded by writing that name in a data file. Before 3.79 twenty-four of them
shipped under no name and could only be reached by adding a case through
\hyperref[doc:uramses]{URAMSES}. The Hydro-Qu\'ebec families (\texttt{models/*/hq/}) and
\texttt{inj\_norton} are excluded from the build entirely and are not reachable by any
route.

\end{docsnote}

\section{The Synchronous Machine}\label{model-index:the-synchronous-machine}

The machine itself is not selected by name; every \texttt{SYNC\_MACH} record uses the same
model, parameterised by the record's own fields.
